events.description: TEXT ORDER entered by Magistrate Judge Douglas J. Quivey on 12/19/2025: Before the Court are Plaintiff's Complaint (Doc. 1 ) and Motion to Compel (Doc. 2 ). Pursuant to Local Rule 11.4(A)(2), "[d]ocuments signed by an attorney must be filed using that attorney's log-in and password; they may not be filed using a log-in and password of another attorney." The Complaint and Motion to Compel were filed using Christopher Gardner's log-in and password but are signed by Brittany Bennett. Therefore, the Clerk is directed to STRIKE the Complaint, (Doc. 1 ), and the Motion to Compel (Doc. 2 ). The Complaint and Motion to Compel, if refiled, must be done so using a signatory's log-in and password. (DW)

events.description: TEXT ORDER entered by Judge Colleen R. Lawless on 3/2/2026: Before the Court are two timely unopposed Motions to Intervene as Defendants. (Docs. 7, 24 ). Under Rule 24(b), a court may permit intervention if a party has "a claim or defense that shares with the main action a common question of law or fact," and doing so will not "unduly delay or prejudice the adjudication of the original parties' rights." Fed. R. Civ. P. 24(b). The Intervenors have established they have "a claim or defense that shares with the main action a common question of law or fact," and this Court finds intervention at this early stage will not "unduly delay or prejudice the adjudication." Pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 24(b), Illinois AFL-CIO, Illinois Alliance for Retired Americans, and Illinois Federation of Teachers' Motion to Intervene as Defendants, (Doc. 7 ), and Common Cause, Illinois Coalition for Immigrant and Refugee Rights, Brian Beals, Pablo Mendoza, and Alejandra L. Ibaez's Motion to Intervene as Defendants, (Doc. 24 ), are hereby GRANTED. The Clerk is DIRECTED to file the proposed Answer, (Doc. 8-4), and Motion to Dismiss, (Doc. 25-1), attached to the respective Intervenors' Memoranda in Support of their Motions to Intervene. (BMG)
